item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=methods+for+detecting+reward+misspecification+in+reinforcement+learning+and+complex+optimization&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6446236\", \"title\": [\"Reward Inference for Portfolio Optimization via Multi-Expert Inverse Reinforcement Learning\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Portfolio optimization requires navigating complex trade-offs among conflicting financial objectives, including return maximization, risk mitigation, and drawdown control. Reinforcement Learning (RL) provides a dynamic framework for asset allocation, but manually specifying reward functions that generalize across diverse market regimes remains a significant challenge. Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) offers a principled alternative by recovering reward signals from expert behavior. However, when demonstrations originate from multiple experts with divergent investment objectives, the collective expert distribution becomes inherently multi-modal. Multiple distinct actions may be simultaneously rational for a given market state, and conventional IRL frameworks are not designed to accommodate this complexity. We propose Multi-Expert Inverse Reinforcement Learning (ME-IRL), a framework that employs an Energy-Based Model (EBM) as a reward network to model this multi-modal collective expert distribution. Rather than specifying objectives a priori or aggregating expert behaviors at the action-level, ME-IRL performs reward-level inference that encodes interactions among conflicting financial objectives. This is achieved through a Transformer-based architecture utilizing cross-attention between state and action representations to explicitly model cross-sectional asset dependencies. Empirical evaluations across ETF and stock portfolios consistently demonstrate that ME-IRL out-performs traditional financial models and single- and multi-objective RL baselines in both return and risk-adjusted metrics across diverse market conditions.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6446236\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.31224/4154\", \"title\": [\"Reinforcement Learning for Financial Portfolio Optimization:  Dynamic Strategies for Risk and Reward Management\"], \"abstrac…
